summary: The agent delivered a substantial, legitimate implementation and preserved the baseline suite, but 10 of 263 new tests failed. The dominant defect is that grouping and sorting reject valid keys when no frame carries the attribute, contrary to the specified missing-attribute grouping/tie behavior; dimension normalization also rejects or skips ragged/missing frame-content cases.
quick_failure_summary: Grouping/sorting mishandles keys absent from all frames, and dimension normalization mishandles missing or ragged index vectors.

details.reasoning: Seven failures come from `_keyed_frames()` requiring each key to occur in at least one effective frame attribute. A valid keyword or tag absent from every frame should instead yield one missing-value group or stable ties; the prompt explicitly says frames carrying none of an attribute group together and missing values sort last. Three further failures come from `_normalise_dimensions()`: it returns without renumbering when no DimensionIndexSequence exists and raises whenever a frame has no FrameContentSequence or a shorter dimension vector, rather than operating on the dimensions/frames that carry values and leaving missing portions alone. The implementation otherwise passes 253 new tests and all 2632 baseline tests.
details.secondary_factors: The phrase `a key naming no attribute` can superficially suggest checking whether the key occurs in any frame, but the later missing-attribute semantics and the distinction between an invalid keyword and a valid tag resolve the intended behavior. The agent's own added test explicitly encoded the incorrect all-frames-absent interpretation.

justification.issue_description: Valid grouping or sorting keys that are absent from every frame are rejected instead of treating every frame as having the same missing value.
justification.evidence: The prompt states that `group_frames` handles `frames carrying none of an attribute grouping together`, that `sort_frames` places `frames missing an attribute after those that have it`, and that keys may be keywords or tags. The visible `Tag` conversion API distinguishes an invalid keyword from a valid numeric tag even when no dataset contains that tag. Nevertheless, `_keyed_frames()` raises whenever `not any(tag in item for item in attributes)`. The prompt also says remaining dimensions are renumbered in first-seen order, while the implementation requires every frame vector to have the full description width.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than a hidden-test mismatch because missing key values were explicitly part of the requested grouping and sorting semantics, and missing/ragged dimension carriers are a foreseeable consequence of optional functional-group content. The hidden tests expose those gaps but do not introduce the core requirement.

problem_assessment.notes: This is a broad, integration-heavy task involving DICOM functional groups, pixel encodings, provenance, normalization, and isolation. The wording `a key naming no attribute` has a minor ambiguity, but the explicit missing-attribute grouping and sorting rules make the tested behavior reasonably knowable. The reference solution demonstrates the task is solvable.

evidence: JUnit reports 2632/2632 baseline tests passing and 253/263 new tests passing, with all 10 failures reaching agent-modified multiframe logic.
The failures are ordinary assertions or `MultiFrameError` exceptions from `src/pydicom/multiframe.py`; there are no import, setup, dependency, or verifier bootstrap errors.

The trajectory shows focused tests passing and a full local suite with one unrelated TLS CA/download failure; the verifier excluded that network test and completed both graded suites, so it did not cause the graded failure.
The agent completed the implementation, added focused tests, and did not spend repeated steps reverting or debugging a shared verifier failure.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker affected grading; the new-test failures are reproducible implementation gaps in key and dimension handling.
